summary: POC scoping focused on integrating Redwood's OpenAI-compatible SDK and endpoints into Aurora Healthcare's triage chat and structured data extraction pipeline. Main goals: validate latency and accuracy for function-calling flows, size throughput for peak-hour triage traffic, and confirm security integration (VPC + KMS + audit logs). Agreed next steps: exchange sample traffic, Redwood to run benchmark scripts, technical walkthrough for private networking and SSO/KMS.
topics: Success criteria: latency SLOs, accuracy for structured outputs, rollout metrics
Workload sizing: qps, tokens per request, concurrency and burst patterns
Benchmarks: streaming vs non-streaming, function-calling latency, prefix/KV cache effects
Integration: OpenAI-compatible SDK, function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs, validation
Security: VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM, SOC2/audit logs, data retention
Timeline: 4-week POC, pilot in staging, pilot->prod gating criteria
transcript:
00:00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the POC scope for integrating our OpenAI-compatible endpoints into Aurora's triage flow.
00:00:12 Samir Khan: yeah thanks, timeboxed, we have about 50 minutes. main thing for us is throughput during peak afternoon triage and making sure function calling returns structured JSON every time.
00:00:28 Diego Alvarez: quick intro from my side, I'm Diego, I'll own the benchmark scripts and the end-to-end latency tests. we typically test both streaming and non-streaming paths because function-calling often uses streaming for token-by-token actions.
00:00:42 Lena Ortiz: just to be clear, our success criteria are: median latency under 300ms for short-turn triage (single-turn prompts), 99th percentile under 1.2s, and structured output schema validation at >= 98% compliance.
00:00:59 Maya Chen: got it. those are reasonable — for hosted endpoints we often hit sub-200ms median for small models, but it depends on quantization/profile. we should size concurrency too. what's your peak qps?
00:01:12 Samir Khan: right now our triage sees about 120 rps sustained between 1pm and 3pm PST, with spikes up to 320 rps for 30s. average tokens/request ~ 180, with function-calls that return ~120 tokens.
00:01:29 Diego Alvarez: ok that maps to ~21k tokens/sec sustained, spikes up to 56k tokens/sec. we'll simulate both steady state and burst. we'll test with and without prefix/KV cache — you mentioned you have a lot of common prefixes?
00:01:44 Samir Khan: yes about 40% of requests share patient-English intro templates, so prefix cache would help.
00:01:50 Priya Desai: small callout on security — we need private deployment options or VPC peering, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also need SOC2 and penetration test artifacts.
00:02:03 Rhea Patel: we can do Private with a customer-controlled VPC, or Dedicated with VPC peering; KMS is supported, HSM for enterprise is an add-on, and audit logs can stream to your S3 or SIEM. I'll attach the runbook for VPC/KMS setup.
00:02:18 Lena Ortiz: for function-calling we want OpenAI-compatible shapes so our front-end code needs minimal changes. will the SDK be drop-in?
00:02:27 Maya Chen: yes the endpoints expose OpenAI-compatible semantics: function call schema, name, args, etc. our JS/py SDKs have shims so migrating calls just needs URL and api-key swap in most cases. there are minor opt params for routing and model pins.
00:02:42 Samir Khan: noise — sorry — is streaming function-calls supported? we need partial outputs as they come in.
00:02:48 Diego Alvarez: yes streaming is supported for the OpenAI-compatible completion route and for function-calls we stream tokens; caveat is that function-calling can be buffered at times based on the kernel selection if the model uses kv caching heavily. we'll test both extremes.
00:03:04 Priya Desai: transcription note: 'kayvee cache' not 'kv cache' — (laughter). but seriously, we need to see determinism around schema adherence, because downstream systems ingest those JSONs into patient records.
00:03:20 Rhea Patel: on schema adherence we recommend an acceptance test that runs 1000 canonical prompts and checks against the validation checklist — we'll provide that script.
00:03:30 Samir Khan: timeline question: how long for a POC? we're thinking 3-4 weeks.
00:03:35 Maya Chen: typical POC is 4 weeks: week 0 setup (networking + creds), week 1 smoke + baseline benchmarks, week 2 tuning (batching, quant, routing), week 3 productionish load tests + accuracy evals, and final wrap with decision. we can compress to 3 if both sides are ready.
00:03:53 Lena Ortiz: for benchmarks, can you outline what you'll run? we need to understand what numbers you'll report.
00:03:59 Diego Alvarez: benchmark suite: 1) single-turn short (<256 tokens) streaming median/99th, 2) function-call roundtrip (end-to-end inc parsing + validation) median/99th, 3) multi-turn with KV cache enabled to see token cost savings, 4) burst stress — 30s spike to 2.5x baseline. we'll produce tokens/sec, latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and schema pass rate.
00:04:31 Priya Desai: also include TLS client auth? we prefer mTLS for service-to-service in VPC.
00:04:37 Rhea Patel: we support mTLS for Private deployments. for hosted we use standard TLS + API key; for Dedicated/Private we can configure mTLS and customer certs.
00:04:48 Samir Khan: dev integration notes — our stack is python backend + node frontend, currently calling OpenAI SDK. we want to swap to Redwood with minimal code changes. can you share migration examples?
00:04:59 Maya Chen: yes we'll share sample snips for python/node. typical pattern: change endpoint to redwood.com/v1/..., set X-Redwood-Client header, and call same function_call parameters. we'll include code for streaming handlers.
00:05:12 Lena Ortiz: question on model selection: do you bring models or do we pick from Open weights?
00:05:18 Diego Alvarez: we host curated open models and maintain performance profiles. for POC we'll propose two candidate models: one optimized for latency (quantized 8-bit) and one for higher quality (fp16). we'll include rollback to a smaller variant if latency SLOs fail.
00:05:33 Samir Khan: and how do rollouts work? we need canary + fallback to openai if Redwood is down.
00:05:40 Maya Chen: rollouts support canary percentages and automatic fallback policies. fallback to OpenAI or internal fallback model is supported as a policy. you'll configure through Redwood Console or via API.
00:05:53 Priya Desai: any PII masking? patient data concerns — we need retention controls and optional in-flight redaction.
00:06:02 Rhea Patel: we have options: no retention for hosted (if you choose), retention at configured TTL for Dedicated, plus field-level redaction plugin you can run pre/post. for Private deployments you can keep everything on-prem.
00:06:17 Samir Khan: good. bench question: cost estimates — we'd like a ballpark for the two candidate models at our expected load.
00:06:25 Diego Alvarez: we'll run a sample run with your traces — that'll give token counts and we can estimate per-1k token costs for each model plus expected throughput footprint. we'll provide a cost math sheet.
00:06:37 Lena Ortiz: about function-calling schema — we'll want strongly typed outputs e.g., {triage_code: string, severity: int, followup_actions: [ {type, owner, eta} ]}. how strict is Redwood about the output? sometimes models add extra fields.
00:06:53 Maya Chen: we offer structured-output post-validation in the pipeline with a strict-mode that rejects non-conforming output. otherwise we surface warnings and a best-effort parse. strict-mode can be a gating criteria for production.
00:07:07 Samir Khan: ok. also interested in autoscaling behavior under burst. how fast can Dedicated scale?
00:07:13 Diego Alvarez: Dedicated autoscaling is configurable; fastest stable scale is usually within 90s for burst capacity if policies are permissive. for sub-200ms tail latencies we recommend pre-warmed reserved slots for critical windows.
00:07:26 Priya Desai: compliance process — legal will need standard DPA + addendum for PHI. any experience with HIPAA customers?
00:07:35 Maya Chen: yes we have HIPAA support for Private deployments and enterprise agreements with BAAs. we'll route legal to customer success to start the DPA conversation.
00:07:46 Lena Ortiz: minor nit: will the SDK surface model explainability or token attribution? we need to debug hallucinations sometimes.
00:07:53 Diego Alvarez: we provide token-level timing breakdowns and per-token logits on request for deeper debugging (subject to model support and cost).
00:08:05 Samir Khan: great. let's talk timeline concretely — we can get sample traces by Monday, security docs by Friday, and we want an initial benchmark by the following Friday. works?
00:08:15 Maya Chen: yes that aligns. we'll send the POC runbook today and Diego will start the benchmark harness once we have traces.
00:08:22 Rhea Patel: I'll drop the function-call validation checklist and sample schemas in the chat.
00:08:27 Priya Desai: question, do you support audit log forwarding to Splunk?
00:08:31 Rhea Patel: yes we can forward to Splunk or S3; we'll include log-format details.
00:08:36 Samir Khan: any blockers on our side for a quick start? we need a short-lived API key and a staging endpoint.
00:08:42 Maya Chen: we'll provision a sandbox key for the POC and grant you staging access to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. note that rate limits in sandbox are conservatively set; they won't reflect dedicated capacity.
00:08:56 Lena Ortiz: good to know. on the bench scripts, can you run a 'schema drift' test that checks fraction of malformed JSONs over time? we had that issue previously.
00:09:07 Diego Alvarez: yes we'll include schema drift and false-positive rates.
00:09:12 Samir Khan: (interruption) quick aside — we use feature flags for rollout; will Redwood signal to our FF system on quality regressions?
00:09:19 Maya Chen: we can integrate alerts or push webhooks to your feature flagging system; we'll propose an A/B gating signal based on schema pass rate and latency.
00:09:30 Priya Desai: can we get a high-level SLO doc for Dedicated? legal will ask for uptime and latency commitments.
00:09:37 Maya Chen: yes Redwood Dedicated comes with SLA templates; I'll attach the SLA doc and the latency tiers we guarantee under reserved capacity.
00:09:46 Lena Ortiz: ok let's capture recap and owners.
00:09:50 Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to share POC runbook, examples, and benchmark scripts (owner: Rhea/Diego). 2) Aurora to provide traces and schema (owner: Samir). 3) Security checklist and docs (owner: Priya). 4) Schedule VPC/KMS walkthrough (owner: Maya).
00:10:10 Samir Khan: agreed. any open questions?
00:10:15 Priya Desai: one more: are there data residency controls? we need EU data to stay in eu-west.
00:10:21 Diego Alvarez: yes region pinning is supported; for Private you choose the region and for Hosted we can route to specific regions depending on your plan. we'll note that in the runbook.
00:10:31 Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts. ending notes: expect the runbook + bench template in the next few hours.
00:10:40 Lena Ortiz: thanks, bye.
00:10:42 (call ends)
